blocks.content: Course: API Handling with Asynchronous Javascript
User input cannot be trusted. Someone might submit an empty form; type a single character; or paste some random text.
If we send bad input to an API, we're wasting a network request and might get useless results in return.
So, we'll write a validateKeyword() function that:

items: Returns both a status and the cleaned data

blocks.content: This pattern of validating before processing is something you'll use in every application you build.
Use this space for your doubts about this lesson. Ask us anything that's confusing and our experts will provide explanations to help you understand.
